items.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: Who were your role models in terms of the bass at that point? Who did you – I would imagine they – you looked up to them, but also . . .

Also would be Oscar Pettiford and people like that that I knew of – great bass players. Slam Stewart. [I] knew about them. And of course, later on, [Jimmy] Blanton with the Duke Ellington band. He was the youngest of all of them. I didn’t ever know him or get to – I only heard him play in person once. I never got a chance to meet him or talk to him, but I heard his records, the stuff that he played on records. He revolutionized the style of the bass in the band. After that came people like Ray Brown and all those…
Can you talk about some of the bands that you played with at this time? This is now moving to the ’30s.
